First, we listen

We understood your brief

What we read in your plansHow we responded
Wardrobes in five locations: Master, Abdullah, the daughter, and Ali’s and Ahmed’s bedrooms.We designed 11 wardrobes made of 31 units — each with its size and purpose — on the exact lines of your plan.
The same model repeats across three villas.One design you approve once, then built three times with the same precision after each villa is surveyed.
L- and U-shaped wardrobes wrapping the walls.No dead corners: an extended rail holds out-of-season clothes, keeping everyday items within reach.
A centre island in the master dressing room (234 × 70).An island with 12 drawers, 3 of them divided for watches, perfume and jewellery.
A vanity with a stool in every dressing room.Three vanities with lit mirrors, next to glass display shelves for perfume.
A 50 cm-deep wardrobe beside the TV wall in Ali’s and Ahmed’s rooms.We kept that depth so the aisle by the bed stays wide, with flush fronts and a finished end meeting the TV wall.
Wardrobes that use the full wall.Top boxes up to the ceiling for luggage and bedding — no dusty gap above the wardrobe.

Options — choose what suits you

Front options

A — Matt lacquer with a touch of glass

Mid-rangeRecommended
Gain: A calm look that keeps dust off; lit glass shows off the bags.
Trade-off: Contents are visible only in the display units.

B — Bronze glass in aluminium frames

Premium
Gain: A boutique feel: see everything at a glance with interior lighting.
Trade-off: Needs to stay tidy, and glass shows fingerprints.

C — Open, no doors

Economy
Gain: Instant access to everything and a wider aisle.
Trade-off: Clothes are exposed to dust; doors remain on top boxes only.
Rayana Wood · ريانة للأخشابWardrobe proposal — Mr. Adnan's villaNovember 2026 · V2 · 35
Options — choose what suits you

Layout, materials & handles

Interior layout

Balanced: hanging 45% · shelves 33% · drawers 22%Mid-rangeRecommended
Suits a wardrobe mixing thobes, abayas and folded clothes.
Trade-off: None — this is the baseline.
More hangingMid-range
For those who iron and hang everything: a shelf unit becomes double hanging.
Trade-off: Less room for folded clothes.
More shelves & drawersMid-range
For T-shirts and sportswear: a hanging unit becomes shelves and drawers.
Trade-off: Less hanging length, slightly higher cost with more drawers.

Front material

MelamineEconomy
Practical and easy to clean.
Trade-off: Fewer colours, simpler look.
HPLMid-range
Resists scratches and moisture.
Trade-off: Edge line is slightly visible.
Matt lacquerMid-rangeRecommended
A smooth, seamless single colour.
Trade-off: Needs care against scratches.
Natural wood veneerPremium
The warmth and touch of real wood.
Trade-off: Natural grain variation, more care.

Handles & extras

Visible gold handleMid-rangeRecommended
Easy to grip and decorative — for dressing rooms.
Trade-off: Projects slightly.
Recessed handleMid-rangeRecommended
Clean lines — for Ali’s and Ahmed’s rooms.
Trade-off: The groove needs cleaning.
Push-to-openPremium
A pure surface, no handle at all.
Trade-off: Mechanism needs periodic adjustment.
Optional extras: Full-length mirror, glass island top to display watches, pull-out ironing board. Sliding doors are not advised for Ali’s and Ahmed’s rooms: depth is 50 cm and sliding needs 65–70.

Why Rayana

Built in Rayana’s own factory

Our own factory in the Eastern Province

We build in-house, not through a middleman — quality and schedule stay in our hands.

Precise cutting & CNC routing

Every part cut to the millimetre, so each unit fits first time.

Machine edge banding

Sealed edges that won’t peel or let moisture in.

Machine boring

Hinges and shelves exactly placed — doors that line up and close quietly.

Design & technical office under one roof

From 3D design to shop drawings, with no detail lost.

What you approve is what gets installed

Drawing, proposal and production order come from one schedule — three villas, one result.
